results.evidence: Both tests in tests/test_actor_stored_everywhere.py passed (2 passed). _run appends --actor founder to every CLI call. The first test runs log-time, log-cost, log-time --voids 1 and log-cost --voids 2. It asserts the rows are time_logged, cost_logged, correction, correction and that every actor is {'founder'}. The second test logs an inbound lead and a call event with --stage researched. It then runs `log-event 1 correction --voids 2` and asserts that the newly written rows are exactly correction and stage_change, both with actor founder. It also asserts that every row in the table has actor founder. 'founder' differs from the default actor (developer), so a dropped --actor would fail the tests. I did not mutate the code to confirm that.
